recipes.name: Slow Cooker Beef Barbacoa
ingredients_raw: 0.5 teaspoon ground black pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Place roast, onion, bay leaves, black pepper, garlic powder, and vinegar in a slow cooker; cover ingredients completely with water. Cover and cook on High setting until meat is very tender and falling apart, about 4 hours.

Remove meat from the slow cooker and discard liquids. Return meat to slow cooker; shred with fork and knife. Stir tomato sauce, chili powder, and salt into the shredded meat. Cover the cooker, and cook meat and sauce on High for an additional 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Beef Barbacoa
raw_recipe.description: This Mexican-style shredded beef is made in the slow cooker until very tender. Wrap some in a flour tortilla for an easy meal.
raw_recipe.name: Slow Cooker Beef Barbacoa

review.reviewBody: This was everything a slow cooker recipe is supposed to be: easy, not a lot of ingredients, and great outcome. Next time, I will probably brown the meat before adding to the slow cooker just to give it another layer of flavor. Great basic recipe that could easily be customized to be more spicy or more intense, depending on your flavor buds. This also would be a great dish to serve at a party - it appeals to many different palates. Thumbs up!

This was delicious! I used chicken broth instead of water and 2 table spoons of real garlic along with 1 tablespoon of garlic powder and 2 extra bay leaves. I put everything in the crock pot at the beginning and did not disturb it for 8 hours. Served with taco, burrito, and tostadas with beans and assorted cheese and toppings

This was delicious. Changed a few things. Instead of a 1/4 cup chili powder mixed in 1 tablespoon of regular chili powder, I tbsp of chipotle chili powder and 1 tbsp. cumin. Also added a few teaspoons of liquid smoke to add authentic bbq flavor. Plus we added a can of diced green chilis. Finally we strained the broth and retained the onions and then added 2-3 tablespoons of broth back in. It. looked a little dry

Very good. I ran out of time to start this on slow cooker mode so instead I pressure cooker it instead for 40 minutes. We then followed the next steps, but reduced the amount of chili powder, added some dashes of chipotle pepper and used the slow cooker mode for 2 hours. Served with tortillas, rice, beans, Mexican blend cheese, and avocado. This made 7-8 servings for a 2 3/4 pound roast.

Made it...used a couple TBSP chipotle and ancho chili powder along with the regular chili powder...i like it spicy. It's was like spicy shredded beef. Very easy ...very tasty...very quick. I keep meaning to buy a timer for my low cooker plug. I would think next time i cook it on low for about 8 hours..timer would make it easier to go to work and not worry about it.

Really good, made some adjustments. Didn't have bayleaf, so I used a roast beef season which has bayleaf ,coriander, garlic salt, also added rotel tomatoes well drained (your choice has to how hot ) along with a teaspoon of liquid smoke or to your liking. Other than that as recipe states. Wife loves it!

THIS WAS AWESOME! I used tomato paste instead of sauce and I swapped the chile powder for 5 dried chipotle meco peppers that I had run through the food processor with the tomato paste.
This tasted exactly like tacos from Chipotle Mexican Grill. I will make this again and again. Just fantastic.

I made this for Father's Day. Every loved it. I did use apple cider vinegar and chopped garlic instead. I cut the onion in thick rings and placed the meat on top of the onions. I also cooked the meat on low for 7 hrs as I had to leave the house. I probably used a tad more meat than called for too. I added a can of chopped green chilies during the last 2 hrs of cooking. I will definitely make this again.

Great recipe!!! I had to alter it to fit into a weeknight menu as most people are not home to stop the cooking process after 4 hours. So what I did was follow the direction my only change was cook my meat on low for 8 hours. After that I followed the directions and returned it back to the crock pot for 1 hour on high... I also added a good amount of garlic salt to the meat when it was cooking on high, it gave it such great flavor.. This is an amazing recipe and tastes so wonderful!!!! You will be so happy you made it!

Made as directed. This was not as spicy as I thought it would be but it was acceptable. It does indeed fall apart and makes a great topping for nachos, cilantro rice, filling for tacos, etc. The vinegar flavor is too strong. I think the recipe should be changed to either remove the vinegar or change they type to red wine / rice etc. and add a dried de-seeded Ancho pepper to steep alongside the bay leaves.

Wow! So freakin good! I did as other users and added extra garlic and cummin. I used Apple cider vinegar since I had no white and I cooked the meat in chicken broth verses water. Amazing!! I just love how easy it was too!
The less ingredients the better is my motto! Simple, easy, and it tastes great. Next time I will add diced bell peppers and onions during second step.

This recipe was good! I added some smoked paprika and 4 ounce can of green chilies, and fresh oregano sprigs just because we had a bunch from garden. I browned the meat in a Dutch oven and then dumped the whole water/spice mixture over it, stirred, put a lid on it and put it in a 300° oven for five hours! Shredded so easily Removed it from the pan, took the bay leaves and oregano out and then. The mixture. Served it on the side to dip or drizzle. I served it with white corn tortillas (browned em a bit on pan with avocado oil) and stacked them on a plate covered them with a lid while they were hot until I had a bunch done. Topped each with chopped onion, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime 🤤

Family enjoyed this for a change to traditional ground beef tacos. Used cider vinegar instead and added a little Cumin to the mix. 2nd time I made this in the InstaPot (40mins) and didn't have any tomato sauce so used red enchilada sauce minimizing the chili powder and vinegar. I was pleasantly surprised how tender it was using an InstaPot! Very nice for when I don't have time to get it into a slow cooker in the morning.
I made this for my grandson. He had discovered Barbacoa while away at College. He loved it!! I sent all of it home with him. Great recipe.

Didn’t chance a thing. Meat was extremely tender. Got good reviews at dinner - considering how simple it is but I was on the fence. Made for our beef burrito bowls. However- had leftovers for lunch the next day and liked more than I did the night before?! Since it was well received and how easy it was, I would make again but I have found/made Barbacoa recipes I like better. Thanks lizbot1!
It’s delicious, at least once a month on my table, the whole family loves it.

I made this recipe for dinner tonight and it was a hit. The only thing I didnt have was vinegar so I substituted it for 1/3 cup of lemon juice. 

I thought it was going to be spicy for my 7 and 2 year is but it wasn't. 

Definitely trying it again!
I made this according to the recipe. The only change I made was I scaled back the chili powder and added more garlic powder. It came out delicious and I will definitely make it again
